 Over one The tour 
 The 2026 tour
 India in New Zealand: the full tour
 Twelve matches from 22 October: five T20Is, five ODIs and two Tests.
 India play five T20Is, five ODIs and two Tests in New Zealand between 22 October and 1 December. It is the largest bilateral tour New Zealand Cricket has ever hosted, and it is set against 100 years of sporting ties between the two countries.
 12 Matches Across six grounds in five cities 2009 India's last Test series win in NZ 1-0 under MS Dhoni 96 Runs India's winning margin in the 2026 T20 World Cup final 3–0 New Zealand in India, 2024 India's first home whitewash in a 3-Test series 
 What each leg is really about
 The T20Is The T20Is are India's first series in New Zealand as double world champions, with Shreyas Iyer now in charge of the side. New Zealand lost the final in Ahmedabad heavily and will want a different story on their own pitches, where the ball swings early and Eden Park's short boundaries punish anything loose.
 The ODIs The ODIs are a meeting of the top two sides in the ICC rankings, a year before the 2027 World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia. New Zealand won the ODI series in India 2-1 in January, so India start this leg with something to put right. Both sides have named separate squads for the first three games and the last two, and Shubman Gill hands the Indian captaincy to Shreyas Iyer for the final two.
 The Tests The Tests carry the most weight. Both count towards the World Test Championship, where India sit fifth, and New Zealand have won the last three Tests between the sides. India have won a Test series in New Zealand only twice, in 1968 and 2009.

 Reading the squads
 India's T20I squad mixes the World Cup-winning core, including Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson, Axar Patel and Varun Chakaravarthy, with new faces. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and Naman Dhir are in, and Bhuvneshwar Kumar returns, his swing likely to be useful with a new ball in New Zealand.
 India have split their ODI squad too. Shubman Gill captains the first three games before he and the Test specialists leave to prepare for Wellington; Shreyas Iyer takes over for the last two. Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli are in for all five. Tilak Varma, Auqib Nabi, Yash Thakur and Kumar Kushagra come in for the final two, and Jasprit Bumrah returns for the Tests.
 New Zealand have split their ODI selection. The first three games lean on experience, with Tom Latham, Devon Conway and Rachin Ravindra. The last two bring in pace and power, with Lockie Ferguson, Finn Allen and Tim Seifert, plus uncapped or lightly capped names such as Kristian Clarke, Mitch Hay and Nick Kelly.

 Head to head: seventy years of the rivalry
 India and New Zealand first played a Test in 1955. The records in Tests, ODIs and T20Is, and the matches that shaped them.
 TOI Sports Desk · Updated 19 October 2026
 New Zealand arrived in India in late 1955 for a five-Test series and lost it 2-0. In Chennai (then Madras), Vinoo Mankad and Pankaj Roy put on 413 for the first wicket. Twelve years later the roles flipped: Mansur Ali Khan Pataudi's side won 3-1 in New Zealand, India's first Test series win abroad.
 Since then the rivalry has swung in long arcs. New Zealand have won the big knockouts as often as India, and India have struggled to win Test series in New Zealand. Start with the numbers, format by format.
 219 Matches Men's internationals since 1955 104 India wins 79 New Zealand wins 3–3 ICC knockouts Level since 2000 
 Three eras of a rivalry
 The Test years
 41 years between India series wins in New Zealand 1968 2009 For four decades this was a Test contest decided by home conditions: turners in India, seam and wind in New Zealand. India's 1968 series win there took 41 years to repeat.
 The one-day years
 63 – 52 ODI wins, India v New Zealand India NZ One-day cricket brought the sides closer. India have won more ODIs, 63 to 52, but New Zealand have tended to rise for the matches that mattered, and since 2019 those have come on the biggest stages.

 Over five The arguments 
 Over five · Great controversies 
 Five moments that still start arguments
 A refused single, a fielding graphic, a send-off, the light and a review. What happened, and why people still disagree.
 Case 01 Hamilton · 10 February 2019 · 3rd T20I 
 The non-strike
 New Zealand won by 4 runs
 The single that wasn't taken
 What happened
 India needed 16 off the last over, chasing 213 for the series. Off the third ball Dinesh Karthik turned down a single and sent back Krunal Pandya, who had 26 off 13 balls. Karthik hit the last ball for six, but India lost by four runs and the series 2-1.
 Why it's still argued
 Karthik said afterwards that he had backed himself to hit a six. Whether the single would have changed the result is still argued over.
 Case 02 Manchester · 10 July 2019 · World Cup semi-final 
 The run-out
 Fact-checks: delivery was legal
 Six outside the circle?
 What happened
 Martin Guptill's direct hit from the deep ran out MS Dhoni and left India needing 25 off nine balls. A broadcast graphic before the delivery seemed to show six New Zealand fielders outside the circle, one more than allowed, and fans called it a no-ball.
 Why it's still argued
 Ball-by-ball checks of the footage found five fielders out, and the graphic was wrong. A batter can be run out off a no-ball anyway. It was Dhoni's last international innings.
 Case 03 Christchurch · 1 March 2020 · 2nd Test 
 The celebration
 Match referee: no action
 The send-off
 What happened
 Virat Kohli greeted Kane Williamson's dismissal with a loud send-off from the slips. When Tom Latham was bowled, he turned to a section of the crowd with a finger to his lips.
 Why it's still argued
 Asked about it after India's seven-wicket defeat, Kohli told the reporter this was not the place to create controversy and said the match referee had no issue. Williamson put it down to Kohli's passion.
 Case 04 Kanpur · 29 November 2021 · 1st Test 
 The last wicket
 Bad light: match drawn
 Saved by the light
 What happened
 Chasing 284, New Zealand were 155 for 9 with about nine overs left. Debutant Rachin Ravindra and No. 11 Ajaz Patel blocked out 52 balls before the umpires took the players off for bad light at 165 for 9.
 Why it's still argued
 India were one wicket from victory in fading light. Stand-in captain Ajinkya Rahane said the umpires had made the right call, and India won the next Test in Mumbai by 372 runs.
 Case 05 Mumbai · 3 November 2024 · 3rd Test 
 The review
 Not out, overturned to out
 Bat, pad or both?
 What happened
 Chasing 147, India were 29 for 5 before Rishabh Pant's 64 off 57 balls brought them back. Given not out caught behind off Ajaz Patel, he was sent off on review after UltraEdge showed a spike.
 Why it's still argued
 The spike came as bat brushed pad, and Rohit Sharma said the bat was clearly close to the pad. India lost by 25 runs, completing New Zealand's 3-0 sweep.
